Prerequisite: Network Advantage license on the switch (on a stack, the active switch, with every member at the same license level)
What it enables: OSPF and BGP (with Network Essentials only default routing, static routing, and RIP run), MSDP, Management Traffic Control, reflexive access lists, and IGMP and MLD snooping over VPLS
How to put it in place: license boot level network-advantage, save the configuration and reload, then check with show license summary
Source: IP Routing Configuration Guide, *Configuring IP Unicast Routing* (supported protocols by license level) and *Configuring MSDP* (Network Advantage feature set); Stacking and High Availability Configuration Guide, *Prerequisites for Switch Stacks*; RN entries marked Network Advantage: *Management Traffic Control* (17.13.1), *Reflexive Access Lists (IPv4)* (17.10.1), *IGMP (IPv4) : VPLS Layer 2 Snooping* (17.1.1), and *MLD Snooping over VPLS* (17.6.1); CR, *license boot level*

Prerequisite: SSH server keys: a hostname, an IP domain name, and an RSA key pair of at least 2048 bits
What it enables: The SSH server (SSH-only VTY lines, the SSH algorithms, NETCONF over SSH) and Secure Copy, which relies on SSH
How to put it in place: hostname <HOSTNAME>; ip domain name <DOMAIN_NAME>; crypto key generate rsa modulus 2048, then check with show ip ssh
Source: Security Configuration Guide, *Prerequisites for Configuring Secure Shell* (RSA key pair, hostname and host domain, encryption image); System Management Configuration Guide, *Prerequisites for Secure Copy*; RN, *Deprecation of Weak Ciphers* (17.11.1: minimum RSA key pair size 2048 bits)

Prerequisite: A management network: the Ethernet management port (GigabitEthernet0/0, a port in the Mgmt-vrf VRF) or a management SVI, with an address and the management subnet defined
What it enables: Management access lists, VTY access classes, Management Traffic Control, and RADIUS testing in a non-default VRF
How to put it in place: interface GigabitEthernet0/0; vrf forwarding Mgmt-vrf; ip address <MGMT_IP_ADDRESS> <MASK>
Source: Interface and Hardware Components Configuration Guide, *Configuring Ethernet Management Port* (prerequisite: assign an IP address; the port is a VRF interface); Cisco TrustSec Configuration Guide, *Cisco TrustSec Overview* (VRF-aware automated tester needs a source interface in the VRF); feature map rows *Management access list on the VTY lines* and *Out-of-band management interface and management ACLs*

Prerequisite: AAA enabled (the AAA new model), with an exec authorization method for Secure Copy
What it enables: AAA common criteria password policies, the enable password policy, AAA login method lists, and the Secure Copy server
How to put it in place: aaa new-model; aaa authorization exec default group RADIUS_GROUP local
Source: CR, *enable password* (aaa new-model and aaa common-criteria policy must be configured before the common-criteria-policy option) and *aaa common-criteria policy* (example); System Management Configuration Guide, *Prerequisites for Secure Copy* (configure SSH, authentication, and authorization)

Prerequisite: Two reachable RADIUS servers (for example Cisco ISE), each with its own shared secret, defined on the switch in a RADIUS server group
What it enables: Administrator authentication with the local account as fallback, 802.1X and MAB, the RADIUS automated tester, and the RADIUS Message Authenticator attribute
How to put it in place: An organization RADIUS service, then aaa new-model; radius server RADIUS1; address ipv4 <RADIUS_1_IP> auth-port 1812 acct-port 1813; key <KEY>; exit; radius server RADIUS2; address ipv4 <RADIUS_2_IP> auth-port 1812 acct-port 1813; key <KEY>; exit; aaa group server radius RADIUS_GROUP; server name RADIUS1; server name RADIUS2
Source: Security Configuration Guide, *Prerequisites for Configuring RADIUS* (RADIUS and AAA must be enabled) and *Configuring IEEE 802.1x Port-Based Authentication* (Cisco ISE as the authentication server); RN, *Message authenticator attribute in RADIUS* (17.18.1); feature map row *AAA with two RADIUS servers and the local account as fallback*

Prerequisite: A TACACS+ server that supports TACACS+ over TLS, and the certificates for the TLS connection
What it enables: TLS for TACACS+
How to put it in place: An organization TACACS+ service with TLS; the 26.x guides give no switch command for it (see *Where the commands come from*)
Source: Security Configuration Guide, *Configuring TACACS+* (prerequisites; feature history: TACACS+ over TLS, 17.18.1, certificate-based AAA services); RN, *TLS for TACACS+* (17.18.1)

Prerequisite: The AAA common criteria password policy PASSWORD_POLICY
What it enables: The local account and the enable password created under the policy, and the added combination rules
How to put it in place: aaa new-model; aaa common-criteria policy PASSWORD_POLICY; min-length 15; upper-case 1; lower-case 1; numeric-count 1; special-case 1; char-change 8
Source: CR, *enable password* and *username*; feature map row *Password policy (AAA common criteria policy)*

Prerequisite: 802.1X authentication on the switch (the dot1x method list and system authentication control), and endpoints with 802.1X client software or MAC addresses known to the RADIUS server for MAB
What it enables: 802.1X and MAC Authentication Bypass on the host-facing ports
How to put it in place: aaa authentication dot1x default group RADIUS_GROUP; dot1x system-auth-control, with an 802.1X supplicant on each endpoint that supports one
Source: Security Configuration Guide, *Configuring IEEE 802.1x Port-Based Authentication* (method list; clients with 802.1x-compliant client software; MAC authentication bypass); feature map row *IEEE 802.1X port-based authentication with MAC Authentication Bypass*

Prerequisite: Two central syslog servers
What it enables: Off-loading log records and alerts to two servers
How to put it in place: Two organization log servers, then logging host <SYSLOG_SERVER_1>; logging host <SYSLOG_SERVER_2>
Source: System Management Configuration Guide, *Configuring System Message Logs*; feature map row *Syslog to two central log servers*

Prerequisite: Authoritative NTP servers that share the authentication key (the same key number and value) with the switch
What it enables: Authenticated time synchronization, and a set system clock for certificate enrollment and validation
How to put it in place: Organization NTP servers with the key, then ntp authenticate; ntp authentication-key 1 hmac-sha2-256 <KEY>; ntp trusted-key 1
Source: System Management Configuration Guide, *Administering the Device* (NTP authentication: the switch synchronizes only to a source that has one of its keys); IP Routing Configuration Guide, *Configuring Multi-VRF CE* (the key number and value must be the same on the client and the server); Security Configuration Guide, *Configuring Secure Socket Layer HTTP* (set the system clock before you configure a CA trustpoint)

Prerequisite: An SNMPv3 manager configured with the same user, authentication, and privacy settings
What it enables: SNMPv3 queries and notifications with SHA authentication and AES privacy
How to put it in place: The organization network management system, then snmp-server host <NMS_IP_ADDRESS> version 3 priv V3USER
Source: Network Management Configuration Guide, *Configuring Simple Network Management Protocol*; feature map row *SNMPv3 with SHA authentication and AES-256 privacy*

Prerequisite: An SCP server and account for configuration backups
What it enables: The EEM applet that copies the running configuration off the switch when it changes
How to put it in place: An organization SCP server; the applet copies to it with a copy running-config command to an scp:// address
Source: System Management Configuration Guide, *Secure Copy*; feature map row *Configuration backup on change (EEM applet and SCP)*

Prerequisite: PKI: a reachable DoD CA enrollment (SCEP) service, the CA certificate authenticated on the trustpoint, and the switch certificate enrolled
What it enables: Certificates from the DoD CA for the switch
How to put it in place: crypto pki trustpoint <TRUSTPOINT>; enrollment url <DOD_CA_ENROLLMENT_URL>; exit; crypto pki authenticate <TRUSTPOINT>; crypto pki enroll <TRUSTPOINT>
Source: Security Configuration Guide, *Configuring Secure Socket Layer HTTP* (Configuring a CA Trustpoint) and *X.509v3 Certificates for SSH Authentication*; Cisco IOS Security Command Reference, *crypto pki authenticate* and *crypto pki enroll*

Prerequisite: The software image for the platform, on flash or on a TFTP, FTP, HTTP, or HTTPS server the switch can reach
What it enables: Installing a supported release
How to put it in place: Copy the image from Cisco to the file server; the install command copies it from the remote location to the switch
Source: System Management Configuration Guide, *Performing Device Setup Configuration* (Software Install: install add file copies the package from a remote location via FTP, HTTP, HTTPS, or TFTP)

Prerequisite: A VTP domain with the same domain name and VTP password on every switch in it
What it enables: VTP authentication (devices without the password, or with the wrong one, reject VTP advertisements)
How to put it in place: vtp domain <DOMAIN_NAME> on each switch, with the same password
Source: VLAN Configuration Guide, *Configuring VTP* (Passwords for the VTP Domain)

Prerequisite: The user, unused, native, and management VLANs created on the switch
What it enables: Per-VLAN settings (DHCP snooping, dynamic ARP inspection), VLAN assignments, trunk native and allowed VLAN lists, and the SVIs
How to put it in place: vlan <VLAN_ID>, then check with show vlan brief
Source: VLAN Configuration Guide, *Configuring VLANs* and *Configuring VLAN Trunks*

Prerequisite: A DHCP server or DHCP relay agent configured and enabled, and the ports toward it trusted for DHCP snooping
What it enables: DHCP snooping, and the bindings that IP Source Guard and dynamic ARP inspection use
How to put it in place: interface <UPLINK_PORT>; ip dhcp snooping trust
Source: IP Addressing Services Configuration Guide, *Prerequisites for Configuring DHCP* (DHCP server and relay agent configured and enabled before DHCP snooping; ports connected to a DHCP server trusted)

Prerequisite: DHCP snooping enabled globally and on the user VLANs
What it enables: IP Source Guard (DHCP snooping must be enabled on the access VLAN) and dynamic ARP inspection (which depends on the DHCP snooping binding database)
How to put it in place: ip dhcp snooping; ip dhcp snooping vlan <USER_VLANS>
Source: Security Configuration Guide, *Configuring IP Source Guard* and *Configuring Dynamic ARP Inspection*; feature map row *DHCP snooping*

Prerequisite: The DHCP snooping binding database agent, with a location for the binding file
What it enables: Keeping the DHCP snooping bindings across a reload (without it, a switch with IP Source Guard or dynamic ARP inspection loses connectivity after a reload)
How to put it in place: ip dhcp snooping database <URL>
Source: IP Addressing Services Configuration Guide, *Configuring DHCP* (DHCP Snooping Binding Database; Enabling the DHCP Snooping Binding Database Agent)

Prerequisite: Static bindings for hosts that do not use DHCP: static IP source bindings for IP Source Guard and ARP access lists for dynamic ARP inspection
What it enables: IP Source Guard and dynamic ARP inspection on ports and VLANs with statically addressed hosts
How to put it in place: ip source binding <MAC_ADDRESS> vlan <VLAN_ID> <IP_ADDRESS> interface <PORT>, and an ARP access list for each VLAN with static hosts
Source: Security Configuration Guide, *Configuring IP Source Guard* (static IP source bindings) and *Configuring Dynamic ARP Inspection* (ARP ACLs in non-DHCP environments); CR, *ip source binding*

Prerequisite: UDLD enabled, in the same mode, on the neighbor device's port
What it enables: Detection of unidirectional links (a UDLD-capable port cannot detect one when the far end is not UDLD-capable)
How to put it in place: On the neighbor switch, enable UDLD in the same mode (normal or aggressive) as this switch
Source: Layer 2 Configuration Guide, *Restrictions for Configuring UniDirectional Link Detection*

Prerequisite: IP routing enabled
What it enables: Routing between VLANs and routed ports, so that ACLs between subnets, perimeter filters, uRPF, routing protocols, VRFs, and multicast routing take effect
How to put it in place: ip routing
Source: IP Routing Configuration Guide, *Configuring IP Unicast Routing* (IP routing is disabled by default and must be enabled before routing can take place)

Prerequisite: IPv6 unicast routing enabled
What it enables: Forwarding of IPv6 traffic, router advertisements, and the IPv6 perimeter filters
How to put it in place: ipv6 unicast-routing
Source: IP Routing Configuration Guide, *Configuring IPv6 Unicast Routing*; IP Addressing Services Configuration Guide, *Configuring HSRP* (ipv6 unicast-routing enables the forwarding of IPv6 unicast datagrams)

Prerequisite: Cisco Express Forwarding enabled
What it enables: Unicast RPF (strict and loose mode)
How to put it in place: ip cef
Source: IP Routing Configuration Guide, *Prerequisites for Unicast Reverse Path Forwarding*; feature map row *Cisco Express Forwarding*

Prerequisite: The egress filter ACL that permits only the enclave's valid source addresses
What it enables: The egress filter and uRPF on internal interfaces
How to put it in place: ip access-list extended EGRESS_FILTER; permit ip <INTERNAL_SUBNET> <WILDCARD> any; deny ip any any log-input
Source: IP Routing Configuration Guide, *Prerequisites for Unicast Reverse Path Forwarding* (configure the egress filtering ACLs before Unicast RPF)

Prerequisite: The routing protocol configured with its neighbors, and the same key, key chain, or password configured on each peer
What it enables: OSPF authentication, BGP peer protection and filters, LDP neighbor authentication, and MSDP peer authentication
How to put it in place: router ospf <PROCESS_ID>; network <NETWORK> <WILDCARD> area <AREA_ID> or router bgp <ASN>; neighbor <EBGP_PEER> remote-as <PEER_ASN>, with the matching key on each peer
Source: IP Routing Configuration Guide, *Configuring OSPF* (all neighboring routers on a network must have the same password) and *Configuring BGP*; IP Multicast Routing Configuration Guide, *Configuring MSDP* (the same password on both MSDP peers)

Prerequisite: A Loopback0 interface with an address that the peers can reach
What it enables: Loopback sources for iBGP, the LDP router ID, and MSDP peering
How to put it in place: interface Loopback0; ip address <LOOPBACK_IP> 255.255.255.255
Source: Feature map rows *BGP peer protection*, *MPLS LDP*, and *MSDP peers* (their commands name Loopback0)

Prerequisite: An MPLS core: MPLS forwarding and LDP on the core-facing interfaces, Cisco Express Forwarding, and the IGP (and MP-BGP for VPN routes) between the PE and P devices
What it enables: LDP settings, TTL propagation, L3VPN VRFs, VPWS, VPLS, and the PE edge protections
How to put it in place: mpls label protocol ldp; interface <CORE_INTERFACE>; mpls ip
Source: Multiprotocol Label Switching Configuration Guide, *Prerequisites for MPLS Virtual Private Networks* (MPLS, LDP, and Cisco Express Forwarding in the network) and *Configuring MPLS Layer 3 VPN over GRE* (LDP and MP-BGP)

Prerequisite: MPLS traffic engineering with RSVP on the core links, over IS-IS or OSPF
What it enables: RSVP-TE message pacing
How to put it in place: mpls traffic-eng tunnels; interface <CORE_INTERFACE>; mpls traffic-eng tunnels; ip rsvp bandwidth
Source: Multiprotocol Label Switching Configuration Guide, *Prerequisites for MPLS Traffic Engineering and Enhancements* (MPLS, Cisco Express Forwarding, IS-IS or OSPF)

Prerequisite: IP multicast routing enabled, with PIM sparse mode and a rendezvous point
What it enables: PIM neighbor filters and boundaries, rendezvous point protection, IGMP join filters on the designated router, and MSDP
How to put it in place: ip multicast-routing; interface <PIM_INTERFACE>; ip pim sparse-mode; exit; ip pim rp-address <RP_ADDRESS>
Source: IP Multicast Routing Configuration Guide, *Configuring PIM* (prerequisites) and *Configuring SSM* (enable IP multicast routing and PIM sparse mode)
